title: Number of Ways to Split Array
summary: Given a 0-indexed integer array nums of length n, find the number of valid splits at index i such that the sum of the first i + 1 elements is greater than or equal to the sum of the remaining elements, and i must be less than n - 1.
statement: Given a 0-indexed integer array nums of length n, find the number of valid splits at index i such that the sum of the first i + 1 elements is greater than or equal to the sum of the remaining elements, and i must be less than n - 1.
constraints: Split only after indices zero through n-2 so both sides are nonempty.
A split is valid when the left sum is greater than or equal to the right sum.
hints: Maintain the total sum and a running left prefix.
At each legal split, right equals total-prefix, so compare without a second scan.
Iterate nums[:-1], update prefix, and count prefix>=total-prefix.
The loop covers every and only legal split index, and the algebra gives its exact two side sums.
editorial: The loop covers every and only legal split index, and the algebra gives its exact two side sums.

tests.explanation: Splits after indices zero and one satisfy left sum at least right sum, giving two.
All three possible splits satisfy the inequality.
